name: Intimacy
oneLine: Candid, game-free exchange between people, with no ulterior motive on either side - Berne's own answer to his book's closing question.
whatYouDid: Across six turns where an old friend kept offering familiar game openings, you stayed out of rescuing, persecuting, and withdrawing long enough for something real and unscripted to actually happen between you.
confusion: People sometimes expect intimacy to feel dramatic, or to arrive as a reward after some big breakthrough. Berne's version is quieter than that: it's just unguarded presence, sustained, with nothing being managed or performed on either side.

expand.definition: Berne closes the book by asking what's actually possible once someone stops needing games to structure their time with other people - his answer is intimacy: a candid, game-free exchange, free of the ulterior transactions that keep Persecutor, Rescuer, and Victim running.
expand.otherFraming: It helps to define intimacy by what it isn't: not rescuing (doing the other person's half of the work), not persecuting (attacking instead of meeting), and not withdrawing (stepping back to stay safe) - whatever is left when none of those three happens is close to what Berne meant.
expand.tryThisToday: Next time someone opens with an old familiar complaint or accusation, try asking one real, curious question before you comfort, correct, or change the subject.
